name: MPU-9250 9-axis IMU (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer)
description: TDK InvenSense 9-axis motion sensor: 3-axis accelerometer (±2/4/8/16 g, 16384 LSB/g at ±2 g), 3-axis gyroscope (±250/500/1000/2000 °/s, 131 LSB/(°/s) at ±250 °/s), die temperature sensor and an AK8963 3-axis magnetometer (0.15 µT/LSB) reached through I2C bypass at 0x0C. Sold as: GY-9250 MPU-9250 module (10-pin: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, EDA, ECL, AD0, INT, NCS, FSYNC) with a 3.3 V regulator, 3.3–5 V supply, I2C address 0x68 (AD0 pulled low; 0x69 with AD0 high).
eli5: Feels tilt, shaking and turning on three axes, and also senses which way magnetic north is, like a phone's motion sensor.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Module supply, 3.3–5 V (on-board 3.3 V regulator feeds the chip)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (SPI SCLK); pull-up to 3.3 V on the module

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (SPI SDI); pull-up to 3.3 V on the module

pins.name: EDA
pins.description: Auxiliary I2C data (master bus for external sensors); leave unconnected

pins.name: ECL
pins.description: Auxiliary I2C clock (master bus for external sensors); leave unconnected

pins.name: AD0
pins.description: Address select (SPI SDO): pulled low on the module = 0x68; tie to 3.3 V for 0x69

pins.name: NCS
pins.description: SPI chip select: leave unconnected or at 3.3 V for I2C; low selects SPI

pins.name: FSYNC
pins.description: Frame sync input, pulled to GND on the module; leave unconnected

buildNotes: WHO_AM_I (0x75) should read 0x71. Many cheap GY-9250 boards carry an MPU-6500 (0x70) or MPU-9255 (0x73); an MPU-6500 has no magnetometer.
The chip may power up asleep: write PWR_MGMT_1 (0x6B) = 0x01 to wake it and select the PLL clock, then wait about 35 ms for valid gyro data.

Read ACCEL_XOUT_H..GYRO_ZOUT_L (0x3B–0x48) in one 14-byte burst: seven big-endian signed words (accel X/Y/Z, temperature, gyro X/Y/Z). At ±2 g and ±250 °/s: 16384 LSB/g and 131 LSB/(°/s); temperature = raw / 333.87 + 21 °C.

For the magnetometer, set BYPASS_EN (INT_PIN_CFG 0x37 = 0x02); the AK8963 then answers at 0x0C. Its axes differ from the accelerometer's (X and Y swapped, Z inverted). The Sparkbench simulator models the accelerometer, gyroscope and temperature only, not the AK8963.
Leave AD0, NCS and FSYNC unconnected for I2C at 0x68; never pull NCS low, which switches the chip to SPI.
Mount the module flat and firmly: at rest Z reads about +1 g and the gyro about 0 °/s (each chip has a small gyro offset; average a few hundred readings at rest and subtract).

driver.code:
# MPU-9250 9-axis IMU (TDK InvenSense), MicroPython driver for I2C.
# From the MPU-9250 product specification (PS-MPU-9250A-01), register map (RM-MPU-9250A-00)
# and the AK8963 magnetometer datasheet (MS1356-E-02):
#   WHO_AM_I 0x75 = 0x71 (MPU-9255 reads 0x73; an MPU-6500 with no magnetometer reads 0x70)
#   PWR_MGMT_1 0x6B (bit 7 H_RESET, bit 6 SLEEP, CLKSEL[2:0]); CONFIG 0x1A; GYRO_CONFIG 0x1B;
#   ACCEL_CONFIG 0x1C; ACCEL_CONFIG2 0x1D; INT_PIN_CFG 0x37 (bit 1 BYPASS_EN)
#   ACCEL_XOUT_H 0x3B .. GYRO_ZOUT_L 0x48: 7 big-endian two's-complement words
#   (accel X, Y, Z, temperature, gyro X, Y, Z)
#   Accel: 16384 / 8192 / 4096 / 2048 LSB/g for +-2/4/8/16 g
#   Gyro: 131 / 65.5 / 32.8 / 16.4 LSB/(deg/s) for +-250/500/1000/2000 dps
#   Temperature: TEMP_degC = (TEMP_OUT - RoomTemp_Offset) / 333.87 + 21, RoomTemp_Offset = 0
# The AK8963 magnetometer sits behind the MPU-9250 at I2C address 0x0C once BYPASS_EN is set.
import time

_SMPLRT_DIV = 0x19
_CONFIG = 0x1A
_GYRO_CONFIG = 0x1B
_ACCEL_CONFIG = 0x1C
_ACCEL_CONFIG2 = 0x1D
_INT_PIN_CFG = 0x37
_ACCEL_XOUT_H = 0x3B
_PWR_MGMT_1 = 0x6B
_PWR_MGMT_2 = 0x6C
_WHO_AM_I = 0x75

_ACCEL_RANGES = {2: (0, 16384.0), 4: (1, 8192.0), 8: (2, 4096.0), 16: (3, 2048.0)}
_GYRO_RANGES = {250: (0, 131.0), 500: (1, 65.5), 1000: (2, 32.8), 2000: (3, 16.4)}

# AK8963 magnetometer
_AK_ADDR = 0x0C
_AK_WIA = 0x00     # reads 0x48
_AK_ST1 = 0x02     # bit 0 DRDY
_AK_HXL = 0x03     # HXL..HZH, little-endian two's complement, then ST2 at 0x09
_AK_CNTL1 = 0x0A   # bit 4 BIT (1 = 16-bit), MODE[3:0]
_AK_ASAX = 0x10    # fuse ROM sensitivity adjustment, readable in fuse ROM access mode


def _s16(hi, lo):
    v = (hi << 8) | lo
    return v - 65536 if v & 0x8000 else v


class MPU9250:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x68, accel_range=2, gyro_range=250):
        """addr: 0x68 with AD0 low (module default), 0x69 with AD0 high.
        accel_range: 2, 4, 8 or 16 g. gyro_range: 250, 500, 1000 or 2000 deg/s."""
        if accel_range not in _ACCEL_RANGES or gyro_range not in _GYRO_RANGES:
            raise ValueError('bad accel_range or gyro_range')
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        time.sleep_ms(100)  # start-up time for register read/write: up to 100 ms after power-up
        who = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(addr, _WHO_AM_I, 1)[0]
        if who not in (0x71, 0x73, 0x70):
            raise OSError('MPU-9250 not found (WHO_AM_I 0x%02X, expected 0x71): check wiring, NCS high' % who)
        self.who_am_i = who
        self._w(_PWR_MGMT_1, 0x80)   # H_RESET: restore default register values
        time.sleep_ms(100)
        self._w(_PWR_MGMT_1, 0x01)   # wake (SLEEP = 0), CLKSEL = 1: PLL if ready, else internal oscillator
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        self._w(_PWR_MGMT_2, 0x00)   # all accel and gyro axes on
        self._w(_CONFIG, 0x03)       # DLPF_CFG = 3: gyro 41 Hz bandwidth, 1 kHz internal rate
        self._w(_SMPLRT_DIV, 0x04)   # 1 kHz / (1 + 4) = 200 Hz output rate
        a_sel, self._a_lsb = _ACCEL_RANGES[accel_range]
        g_sel, self._g_lsb = _GYRO_RANGES[gyro_range]
        self._w(_GYRO_CONFIG, g_sel << 3)    # GYRO_FS_SEL, FCHOICE_B = 00 (DLPF in use)
        self._w(_ACCEL_CONFIG, a_sel << 3)   # ACCEL_FS_SEL
        self._w(_ACCEL_CONFIG2, 0x03)        # A_DLPFCFG = 3: accel 44.8 Hz bandwidth
        time.sleep_ms(50)  # gyro data valid about 35 ms after start, accel about 30 ms
        self._mag_adj = None

    def _w(self, reg, val, addr=None):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr if addr is None else addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def raw(self):
        """(ax, ay, az, temp, gx, gy, gz) raw counts from one 14-byte burst (same sample)."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _ACCEL_XOUT_H, 14)
        return tuple(_s16(d[i], d[i + 1]) for i in range(0, 14, 2))

    def read(self):
        """((ax, ay, az) in g, (gx, gy, gz) in deg/s, temperature in deg C)."""
        r = self.raw()
        a = (r[0] / self._a_lsb, r[1] / self._a_lsb, r[2] / self._a_lsb)
        g = (r[4] / self._g_lsb, r[5] / self._g_lsb, r[6] / self._g_lsb)
        return a, g, r[3] / 333.87 + 21.0

    def acceleration(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def gyro(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[2]

    # ---- AK8963 magnetometer (MPU-9250 / MPU-9255 only, not on MPU-6500 clones) ----
    def _mag_init(self):
        self._w(_INT_PIN_CFG, 0x02)  # BYPASS_EN: host talks to the AK8963 directly at 0x0C
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        wia = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(_AK_ADDR, _AK_WIA, 1)[0]
        if wia != 0x48:
            raise OSError('AK8963 magnetometer not found (WIA 0x%02X): board may be an MPU-6500' % wia)
        self._w(_AK_CNTL1, 0x00, _AK_ADDR)   # power-down before changing mode
        time.sleep_ms(1)                     # at least 100 us
        self._w(_AK_CNTL1, 0x0F, _AK_ADDR)   # fuse ROM access mode
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        asa = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(_AK_ADDR, _AK_ASAX, 3)
        # Hadj = H * ((ASA - 128) * 0.5 / 128 + 1); 16-bit output = 0.15 uT/LSB
        self._mag_adj = tuple(((a - 128) * 0.5 / 128 + 1) * 0.15 for a in asa)
        self._w(_AK_CNTL1, 0x00, _AK_ADDR)   # power-down again
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        self._w(_AK_CNTL1, 0x16, _AK_ADDR)   # BIT = 1 (16-bit), continuous measurement mode 2 (100 Hz)
        time.sleep_ms(10)

    def magnetic(self):
        """(mx, my, mz) in microtesla, in the AK8963's own axes (X/Y swapped, Z inverted vs the accel)."""
        if self._mag_adj is None:
            self._mag_init()
        for _ in range(20):
            if self.i2c.readfrom_mem(_AK_ADDR, _AK_ST1, 1)[0] & 0x01:  # DRDY
                break
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(_AK_ADDR, _AK_HXL, 7)  # HXL..HZH plus ST2 (reading ST2 is required)
        if d[6] & 0x08:
            raise OSError('AK8963 magnetic sensor overflow')
        h = [_s16(d[i + 1], d[i]) for i in (0, 2, 4)]
        return tuple(h[i] * self._mag_adj[i] for i in range(3))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mpu9250 import MPU9250

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
imu = MPU9250(i2c)
while True:
    (ax, ay, az), (gx, gy, gz), t = imu.read()
    print('A=%.2f,%.2f,%.2f g G=%.1f,%.1f,%.1f dps T=%.1fC' % (ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, t))
    time.sleep(1)
